title: Additional Support Measures in Response to Elevated Safe Distancing Measures
what_it_is: Additional Support Measures in Response to Elevated Safe Distancing Measures

sections.label: Global COVID-19 spread and lockdowns
sections.summary: As of 5 April 2020, COVID-19 spread to over 200 countries, infected over 1 million and killed over 60,000, with 3.9 billion people on lockdown.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: As of 5 April 2020, COVID-19 has spread to more than 200 countries and territories, infecting over 1 million people and taken more than 60,000 lives.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Today, to control the spread of the virus, more than 3.9 billion people, or half of humanity, are on lockdown.

sections.label: Total infection cases
sections.summary: As of yesterday, there were a total of 1,309 infection cases.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: As of yesterday, we have a total of 1,309 infection cases.

sections.label: Resilience Budget support commitment
sections.summary: The Resilience Budget committed $48 billion to support workers, protect livelihoods, and help enterprises overcome immediate challenges.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: In the Resilience Budget, the Government committed $48 billion to support workers, protect livelihoods, and help enterprises overcome immediate challenges.

sections.label: Solidarity Budget wage subsidy increase
sections.summary: The Solidarity Budget raises the wage subsidy for all firms to 75% of gross monthly wages for the first $4,600 paid in April 2020 per local employee.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: In this Solidarity Budget, I will raise the wage subsidy for all firms to 75% of gross monthly wages, for the first $4,600 of wages paid in April 2020, for each local employee.

sections.label: Jobs Support Scheme payout brought forward
sections.summary: The first Jobs Support Scheme payout is brought forward from May to April 2020 due to pressing cash needs of businesses.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: I understand the cash needs of businesses are very pressing in this difficult period.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Hence, our agencies have been working very hard, to now bring forward the first Jobs Support Scheme payout from May to April 2020.

sections.label: Foreign Worker Levy waiver and rebate
sections.summary: Monthly Foreign Worker Levy due in April is waived for four weeks, and employers get a $750 rebate per work permit or S Pass holder based on 2020 levies.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: To ease the labour costs of such firms during these four weeks I will waive the monthly Foreign Worker Levy due in April.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: To help them preserve their business structure and quickly resume operations, we will also provide employers with a Foreign Worker Levy Rebate of $750 for each work permit or S Pass holder, based on previous levies paid in 2020.

sections.label: Enhanced loan risk share
sections.summary: Government raises its risk share of loans under three schemes from 80% to 90% for loans initiated 8 April 2020 to 31 March 2021.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: To provide additional support on credit, I will further enhance financing support for enterprises so that viable businesses can continue to have access to credit despite the uncertainty.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: I will increase Government’s risk share of loans made under the Temporary Bridging Loan Programme; the Enterprise Financing Scheme – SME Working Capital Loan; and Enterprise Financing Scheme – Trade Loan from 80% to 90% for loans initiated from 8 April 2020 till 31 March 2021.

sections.label: SME loan relief eligibility
sections.summary: More than $40 billion of SMEs' existing loans are likely to qualify for this relief.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: More than $40 billion of SMEs’ existing loans are likely to qualify for this relief.

sections.label: Self-employed income relief scheme
sections.summary: SIRS is extended to self-employed persons with small employment income and the Annual Value threshold is raised, making about 100,000 eligible for three $3,000 payments from May 2020.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: First, I will extend SIRS to automatically include self-employed persons who also earn a small income from employment work.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Second, I will raise the current Annual Value threshold up from $13,000 to up to $21,000, to include those who live in some condominiums and other private properties.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: With these enhancements, a total of about 100,000 self-employed persons will automatically be eligible for the scheme and will receive three payments of $3,000 each, starting from May 2020.

sections.label: Solidarity Payment for Singaporeans
sections.summary: All adult Singaporeans will receive a one-off Solidarity Payment of $600 in cash.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: All adult Singaporeans will receive a one-off Solidarity Payment of $600 in cash.

sections.label: Mental health hotline and costs
sections.summary: Mental health professionals and trained volunteers help set up a new hotline; the measures cost $5.1 billion, with $4 billion for businesses and workers and $1.1 billion for the Solidarity Payment.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: In this time of need, I am glad that mental health professionals and trained volunteers have stepped forward to offer their help in setting up the new hotline.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: These additional measures will cost $5.1 billion, with $4 billion for the additional support for businesses and workers, and $1.1 billion for the Solidarity Payment.

sections.label: Drawing on past reserves
sections.summary: The President's in-principle support was sought and obtained to draw an additional $4 billion from past reserves for support to save jobs and assist Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: These measures will impact our workers and businesses severely; additional support will be required to save jobs, preserve capabilities and provide immediate direct assistance to Singaporeans to help them tide through this exceptional and difficult period.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Therefore, I have sought and obtained the President's in-principle support to draw on an additional $4 billion from past reserves.

sections.label: COVID-19 response and budget deficit
sections.summary: The Government's COVID-19 response totals $59.9 billion, about 12% of GDP, and the FY2020 Overall Budget Deficit rises to $44.3 billion, or 8.9% of GDP.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Taken together, the Government's response to COVID-19 will total $59.9 billion, or about 12% of GDP.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: The Overall Budget Deficit for FY2020 will increase to $44.3 billion or 8.9% of GDP.

sections.label: Solidarity Budget assistance
sections.summary: A $5.1 billion Solidarity Budget will be presented to provide more assistance to people, apart from two previously announced Budgets.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: In order to provide more assistance to our people, apart from the previously announced two Budgets, I will present a $5.1 billion Solidarity Budget.

sections.label: Job Support Scheme wage subsidy
sections.summary: The wage subsidy of the Job Support Scheme in April will be raised from 25% to 75%.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: For this, I will raise the wage subsidy of the Job Support Scheme in April from 25% to 75%.

sections.label: Honesty, trust and circuit breaker
sections.summary: The Government is honest about uncertainties, challenges and costs, and with Singaporeans' trust has taken bold swift actions; the circuit breaker requires everyone to adjust routines, mindsets and habits.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: We are honest about the uncertainties and challenges ahead and honest about the price we need to pay for what we need to do.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: We have been able to take bold and swift actions because we have the trust of Singaporeans, painstakingly built up over the years by delivering for Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: With the circuit breaker in place for the next one month, everyone will have to adjust and adapt not just our physical routines, but our mindsets and habits.

sections.label: Stemming escalating infections
sections.summary: Everyone must do their best to stem escalating infections so the healthcare system is not overwhelmed.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Each and every one of us must do our best to stem the escalating infections to prevent our healthcare system from being overwhelmed.

sections.label: Staying connected while distancing
sections.summary: People may not physically visit extended families and close friends but can connect by phone or video, and the nation can pull close together while physically distancing to save lives.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: We may not be able to physically visit our extended families and close friends but we can stay in touch and connect through phone or video.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: I am confident that we can and will pull close together as a nation even as we physically distance ourselves to save lives.
